answer: An agent marketplace grants each identity one vote while it maintains a 100-token bond, with a 30-day withdrawal delay. Agents named zenith, opal, and lantern face the same rule. Creating 1,000 voting identities therefore ties up 100,000 tokens, and exiting leaves that capital locked for another month. Cheaply generating keys cannot cheaply multiply influence: the attacker must fund every extra vote and sacrifice other uses of the money.
